title: Black Bird
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Misao, a high schooler who can see spirits, is attacked on her sixteenth birthday and saved by childhood friend Kyo, the tengu clan heir, who is also a teacher at her school. She is the 'Bride of Prophecy' whose blood and flesh grant demons power, so clans fight over her while Kyo claims her as his bride. An 18-volume shojo supernatural romance that won the 54th Shogakukan Manga Award.
life_message: Holds up devoted, protective love and motherhood as worth any risk, though reviewers question the relationship's balance.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kyo and rivals settle claims to Misao by combat, including a killing duel.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Prophecy and clan rules bind Misao's fate.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Clan loyalty and family succession drive the plot.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Clan heads, heirs and a destined bride; Kyo dominates the relationship.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Prophecy, the Senkaroku and demon clans guide events.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Security under Kyo's protection valued over Misao's independence.

folkways.japan: Tengu and kitsune clans come from Japanese folklore; the destined-bride and clan-succession frame reflects traditional household (ie) norms.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers critique the romance itself (ANN; Manga Critic via Wikipedia), not preachiness; story carried by melodrama.
delivery.note: The romance is presented as ideal; critics, not the story, raise the questions about power and age.

winners_losers: Misao and Kyo win a happy family ending after she survives childbirth. The story sympathizes with Kyo; reviewers sympathize more with Misao.
